glossary: Anti-Aircraft

Weapons with the Anti-Aircraft rule do not suffer the normal -2 modifier when rolling to hit against targets with the Fly Keyword and any dice that score natural 8s when rolling to hit, score hits as normal.
Anti-Grav

Units with the Anti-Grav Keyword may move over any other Bases or terrain up to Height 4 without penalty (they don't have to move round them). They will still be affected by Difficult Terrain as normal if starting or ending their move within it. They must still respect Unit Coherency and proximity rules once they finish moving and cannot end their move on or inside Impassable terrain. Units with this Keyword may also exit from a transport Vehicle that has the Fly Keyword. [Errata v1.2]
APC

APCs are lightly armoured with basic weapons, designed for getting troops into combat and not much else. Units with the APC keyword have US0. They cannot move to engage and Assault an enemy Unit that has an Action Token (e.g. is still to activate in the Movement phase). In addition, Infantry and Heavy Infantry Units get a +1 to hit modifier and also AP (+1) against them in an Assault (i.e. gain AP1 or increase AP by 1 if it the Unit's attacks already have it).
Armour Penetration (APn)

Armour Penetration is expressed as AP and a number, e.g. AP1, AP2. The number is a positive modifier to the damage roll in both shooting and Assault. For example, if a Unit that has an Armour value of 7+ is hit by weapons that have AP2, the firer will add +2 to their damage rolls, needing just 5+ to damage the target.
Aura [x]

Units with the Aura keyword, and friendly Units while they are within 6" of the Aura Unit, have the keywords specified in brackets. Sometimes a non-keyword stat value will be used, e.g. Save (7+), in which case, all friendly Units within the Aura have this stat value. The Aura Keyword cannot be used while the Unit with it is embarked within a Unit of transport vehicles. 46
Blast (n)

Units with weapons with this Keyword can hit targets in a large area using one or more Blast Templates. See the rules on page 27. All weapons firing with the Blast keyword also have the Sustained Attack keyword (see page 50). Typically, each Blast weapon places a single template, but if its keyword has an n value (e.g. Blast 2), a template is placed for the value of n from each of the firing Bases in the Unit.
Capacity (n)
Units with this Keyword are normally Vehicles that can transport Infantry units. Each transport vehicle in the unit can carry a number of Infantry or Heavy Infantry bases equal to n.
Chained Barrage

Units with this Keyword that fire Blast weapons, may place additional templates next to any previously placed template in this attack, not just the original one. Select the template to connect to before rolling the Targeting Die. If a HIT is rolled for the third (and further) templates in a chained barrage they CAN be deliberately placed over any Command Units or over Unit(s) engaged in an Assault. [Errata v1.2]
Command Radius (n)

Strategic Orders can only be used on friendly Units within the Command Radius (in inches) of a friendly Command Unit (at least one Base needs to be within range). Strategic Orders can be used on the Command Unit itself. Units out of the Command Radius of every friendly Command Unit cannot have Strategic Orders played on them.
Corrosive

If a Unit loses one or more Bases to damage caused by any weapons with the Corrosive Keyword, place a Status Marker on the Unit as a reminder. At the end of the Round, in the "Trigger ‘End phase' special rules" step, roll a single die. If the result beats the Armour value of the affected Unit, one point of damage is caused. No other Keywords are applied (no AP, Vicious etc.), but Save rolls and Resilience Tokens can be used as normal to prevent this by the target Unit. The Status Marker is then removed.
Cunning (Command units only)

In the Command phase, after both players have revealed their Action Tokens, you can change the token of one of your units within Command Radius of this unit, including the mandatory Advance token on any Pinned unit. Other mandatory Action Tokens cannot be changed. If both players have Cunning units, alternate changing tokens starting with the player who does NOT have the Initiative. If you are using the Fog of War game variant, you can use Cunning to change the token of one of your units within Command Radius of this unit, when it is revealed.
Demolisher
Weapons with this Keyword can damage and take down buildings. See Buildings and Shooting on page 38.
Drop-troop
Units with this Keyword may exit from a transport Vehicle that has the Fly Keyword.
Fly

Units with the Fly Keyword operate above the battlefield and suffer less restriction of movement than their counterparts on the ground. They have a Height of 6 above the terrain level they are over. Flyers above this height cannot interact with ground targets meaningfully in the context of the game. This means that flyers may well have to steer around buildings. See page 44. [Errata v1.2]
Heavy Armour
When firing at a Unit with the Heavy Armour Keyword, weapons that do not have the Armour Piercing (AP) Keyword half the number of dice the Unit rolls to damage the target, rounding up. [Errata v1.2]
Hover Deployment
Flying Units with this Keyword may slow to deploy embarked troops (see page 45).
Ignores Cover
Shots from weapons with this Keyword ignore the In Cover to-hit modifier. All weapons firing with the Ignores Cover keyword also have the Sustained Attack keyword (see page 50).
Indirect
Units with weapons with this Keyword may fire Blast weapons indirectly (see page 27).
Indirect (only)
Units with weapons with this Keyword must always fire Blast weapons indirectly (see page 27).
Orbital (or Subterranean) Deployment

Units with these Keywords may deploy from Reserves (see page 58) directly onto the table, rather than coming on from an edge. They (and any Unit they are transporting) may be put into Reserve, even in Scenarios that wouldn't normally allow it. To activate and deploy the Unit, first you must give it an Advance or Sprint Action Token in the Command phase, then in the Movement phase, pick a point on the table and place a Blast Template on it. It must be more than 1" from any other Unit, building or other impassable terrain. Roll the Targeting Die. If a HIT is rolled, the template lands on target. Otherwise move the template the distance shown on the dice in the direction of the die is pointing, stopping if it reaches any other Units, buildings, the edge of the table or Impassable terrain. Now place all the Bases from the Unit on the table, fully or partially on top of the Blast Template, in coherency, and at least 1" from enemy Units (see diagram). Any Bases that cannot be placed in this way are destroyed. If the Blast Template scattered and stopped before it would have hit another Unit, building, edge of the table or Impassable terrain, the Unit (and any Units embarked within it) receive a Pin marker. 47
Pinning
Units with weapons with this Keyword will put a Pin marker on the target so long as at least one hit is scored when shooting at it (even if no casualties are caused).
Primary Weapon

Weapons (or groups of the same named weapons in a Unit with multiple Bases) with this Keyword can each select a target independently (i.e. it can then be the same or a different target from the Unit's other weapons (or groups of weapons)). Declare all targets before resolving any attack. If a Unit is firing more than one identical Primary Blast Weapon at the same target, place the initial template as normal, and then one additional template for each additional (n) of all of the additional Primary Weapon firing at the same target.
Quick-fix (types)

Units with this keyword are able to provide battlefield repairs (or first aid!) to other Units of the listed types. The Quick-fix Keyword cannot be used while the Unit with it is embarked within a Unit of transport vehicles. While a Unit of one of the listed types is within 6" of a friendly Unit that has the Quick-fix keyword and type listed, casualties suffered by Unit are not applied until the end of the Round (in the end phase, as the very first thing in the "Trigger ‘End phase' special rules" step). Note that units with the Fly keyword, and units that are engaged in an Assault, are unable to benefit from the Quick-fix rule. Put a Status Marker down, or track on a different coloured die, for each Base that is temporarily "saved" in this way. This means that the Bases in the Unit that would otherwise have been removed may still act normally until the end of the Round when they are finally removed. You don't have to track the exact Bases, just the number that have delayed death. Note that a Unit can only be allocated a single ‘Quick- fix' Status Marker per Base it has. If the unit takes additional damage (either from a single attack or attacks from different enemies), so that units with these Status Markers would need to be removed as casualties, they are removed immediately as normal. (There is only so much quick-fixing that can help against overwhelming firepower!). Each Base in the Unit only gets one stay-of-execution… Also note that this only applies to Bases that would be removed while the Unit with Quick-fix is in range. If any Bases subsequently take damage while not within range of a Battlefield Repair Unit, they are removed immediately as normal. For example, a Unit of Infantry suffers two points of damage, but is in range of a Unit with the Quick-fix (Infantry, Heavy Infantry) Keyword. Instead of removing two Bases, the player places two Status Markers on the Unit. Later that Round, all the Bases in the Unit shoot at an enemy target, but then it suffers another Point of damage from return fire. It is no longer within the range of the Quick-fix unit, so a Base is removed immediately. In the end Phase at the end of the Round, two more Bases are removed from the Unit.
Resilience (n)

A Unit with the Resilience (n) keyword starts the game with n Resilience shield tokens. Whenever the unit would suffer any amount of damage from a single attack (shooting from a single enemy unit or all simultaneous attacks in an assault), and after any Save rolls, but before Nerve tests in Assaults, spend Resilience Tokens the Unit has instead of taking damage caused by that attack. Each Resilience Token spent can prevent up to two points of Damage from affecting the unit (i.e. the Damage is negated and not applied/ suffered). A Unit must spend as many Tokens as possible to prevent as much damage as possible. Once the last Token has been spent in this way, the Unit can then be damaged as normal. For example, a Unit with 1 Resilience Token is hit and will suffer 3 damage. The Token is removed to prevent 2 of the damage getting through, so the Unit only suffers a single point of damage. Note that if the Unit had only suffered 1 damage, the Token would still have been spent to prevent it. Any "unused" portion of a Token cannot be saved for later! Note that in a multiple assault, all attacks and damage are considered to occur simultaneously, so first determine all the potential damage caused to the Resilient Unit, and then spend the tokens to negate as much of it as possible.
Scout

Units In Play with this Keyword may make a free move, up to their second (Sprint) SP value, after both players have finished deploying their armies, and before the Roll for Command in Round 1. The move follows all the normal rules for movement but cannot be into base-to- base contact with any enemy models. If both players have Units with Scout, they alternate moving them starting with the player that won the Recon roll (see page 57). Units embarked in transport vehicles cannot make Scout moves. If transport Vehicles have the Scout Keyword, any Units inside may not disembark during the scout move. 49
Stealthy
Units shooting ranged weapons at enemy targets with this Keyword suffer a -1 modifier when rolling to hit.
Strider

Units with the Strider Keyword may move over any other Bases or terrain up to Height 3 without penalty (they don't have to move round them). They treat Difficult Terrain as Open Terrain for moving. They must still respect Unit Coherency and proximity rules once they finish moving, and cannot end their move inside Impassable terrain.
Subterranean Deployment
This Keyword follows the same rules as Orbital Deployment – just from the opposite direction!
Sustained Attack
When attacking with weapons with this Keyword all rolls to hit have the Exploding 8! mechanic.
Tactician (dice)
While it is In Play, a Unit with this Keyword adds the indicated Command dice to its side's Command Points roll in the Command Phase. 50
Targeting Systems
A Unit with this Keyword that is shooting a Blast weapon Indirectly, may re-roll the Targeting Die when rolling to place the initial template. The second result stands.
To the Death
Bases in a Unit with this keyword can never be removed as a result of failed Nerve tests when losing an Assault.
Unflinching

A Unit with this Keyword can never be given a Pin marker, so can never be Pinned. Note that this keyword has no impact on Nerve tests, as Unflinching units can still be overwhelmed and cut down when defeated in close quarters.
Vicious
When attacking with weapons with this Keyword all rolls to damage have the Exploding 8! mechanic.
